key_insight: The paper shows that steady lid-driven cavity flows can be computed robustly by iterative linearization and then assessed for stability through an eigenvalue problem on perturbations.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical FEM-based workflow for determining whether high-Reynolds-number cavity flow solutions are physically stable before using them in design or validation studies.
method: Linearize the nonlinear convective terms iteratively, solving one linear boundary-value problem per step.
Discretize the steady flow and perturbation equations with finite elements on triangular meshes.
Form a generalized algebraic eigenvalue problem and check whether any eigenvalues have positive real part.
evidence_signal: The approach was tested on a sequence of refined meshes over a range of Reynolds numbers for square-cavity flow, with stability judged from the computed eigenvalues.
watch_item: Stability conclusions depend on mesh refinement and the accuracy of the linearized eigenvalue solve, so coarse discretizations may miss weak unstable modes.
paper_title: Stability analysis of the steady solution for incompressible lid-driven cavity flow
